chunks: And Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled concerning six people who were in the water, and one man from among them drowned.
Then three of them testified against two that those two had drowned him, and two testified against three that those three had drowned him.

So he obligated all of them to pay the diyyah. He made the two liable for three shares based on the testimony of the three against them, and he made the three liable for two shares based on the testimony of the two against them.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَا: The Commander of the Faithful, Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام
key_terms.الدِّيَةَ: Blood money, the financial compensation due for wrongful killing
key_terms.الْمَاءِ: The water in which the drowning occurred
key_terms.بِشَهَادَةِ: On the basis of testimony or witness evidence

ai.seo_question: How did Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام rule when a drowning case involved conflicting testimony among several people?
ai.summary: This hadith records a judicial ruling of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام in a drowning case involving conflicting testimony among a group. The ruling apportions the diyyah across all implicated parties according to the number of witnesses testifying against each side, showing a precise legal method in adjudicating shared liability.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5233 - The Commander of the Faithful (as) ruled in the case of six people who were in the water, and one of them drowned. Three of them testified that two others had drowned him, while the two testified that the three had drowned him.
Imam (as) obligated all of them to pay the blood money (diyyah).

Imam (as) made the two responsible for three shares of the diyyah based on the testimony of the three against them, and he made the three responsible for two shares based on the testimony of the two against them.
